assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full; driver_capability: ready (confidence 0.75 — the two-session-row half is structural and certain; the PID-binding half is code-derived and depends on an ordering assumption that only a live recording settles).

## agent_supports = yes

Copilot mints a FRESH session UUID per launch and gives each session its own directory, `$COPILOT_HOME/session-state/<uuid>/`. Nothing about session identity is keyed on the working directory, so two concurrent REPLs in one cwd are two independent sessions by construction — the sessions themselves cannot collide.

The one thing that could block concurrency is a lock, and Copilot's lock is session-scoped, not workspace-scoped. In the shipped `app.js` bundle the create path runs `let y = nf(p.sessionId, d), S = await this.registerSessionLock(p.sessionId, y); p.alreadyInUse = S`, and `registerSessionLock(e, n) { return await h.inUseLocksRegisterSession(e, n, process.pid) }`. Every lock primitive in the bundle is session-keyed — `inUseLocksRegister`, `inUseLocksRegisterSession`, `inUseLocksRelease`, `inUseLocksReleaseAllSessions`, `inUseLocksReleaseSession`, `inUseLocksSweep` — and `checkSessionsInUse({sessionIds})` queries by session id. A grep of the whole bundle for `workspaceLock` / `lockWorkspace` / `directoryLock` / `cwdLock` returns nothing. The only "already running for: ${this.targetWorkspaceFolder}" string belongs to an in-process re-entrancy guard on the IDE lock-file watcher (`start(){ if(this.watcher) return … }`), not a cross-process exclusion.

So two fresh launches take two different locks and neither observes `alreadyInUse`. `alreadyInUse` is a per-session flag surfaced on the resume path, not a launch veto.

## daemon_capability = full

| Scenario assertion | Adapter mechanism |
|---|---|
| "Two distinct sessions appear, each with its own session_id" | `Source: FilesUnderRoot{Dir: sessionsDir(), SessionIDFromPath: sessionIDFromPath}` (agent.go / adapter.go). The id IS the `<uuid>` directory name, and Copilot mints a new directory per launch — two launches, two watched `events.jsonl` files, two rows. Nothing here is cwd-keyed. |
| "Each session's state transitions independently — no flapping between rows" | `JSONLineParser{NewParser: func() agent.LineParser { return &Parser{} }}` constructs a FRESH stateful `Parser` per transcript file, so session A's `user.message` / `assistant.turn_end` can never mutate session B's state. Copilot's turn boundaries are explicit (`assistant.turn_start` / `assistant.turn_end`), so neither arc is inferred from a heuristic that could straddle two sessions. |
| "Each session has its own PID; the binding is stable and does not cross-contaminate" | The crux — see below. |

### The crux: cwd-based PID discovery with two candidates

`copilot/pid.go` is `DiscoverPIDByCWD(ProcessName, cwd, disambiguate)` — purely cwd-based, with no argv filter and no sidecar. Two concurrent sessions in the SAME cwd therefore BOTH match `narrowByCWD`, and the disambiguator decides. It resolves correctly, for three reasons that hold together:

1. **The disambiguator is claim-aware, not naive.** `PIDManager.claimAwareDisambiguate` (pid_manager.go) picks the highest UNCLAIMED pid among the cwd matches, falling back to the highest claimed pid only when every candidate is already taken. `narrowByCWD`'s own default (`highestPID`) is never reached, because `TryDiscoverPID` always passes the claim-aware closure.
2. **This exact shape is regression-tested at the services layer, adapter-agnostically.** `session_detector_pid_test.go` drives two `EventNewSession`s with the SAME `CWD`, waits for the first PID to bind so the second discovery sees it claimed, and asserts `stateA.PID != stateB.PID`, `stateA.PID == 1001` ("highest unclaimed"), `stateB.PID == 1000` ("1001 already claimed"). Copilot reaches that code through the identical `DiscoverPIDByCWD` path kiro-cli and mistral-vibe use, so the test covers copilot's crux directly.
3. **Once bound, the binding is immutable for the session's life.** `TryDiscoverPID` returns early when `state.PID > 0`, so the re-drive of session 1 while session 2 is alive does no rediscovery at all — the phase that proves non-cross-contamination cannot regress through the discovery path.

Walking the recipe's ordering concretely: session 1 launches (pid1); the scanner mints `proc-<pid1>`; the first prompt materializes `events.jsonl` and the real session binds pid1 (the only cwd candidate), and `cleanupStalePIDHolders` / `cleanupPreSessionsForProject` retire `proc-<pid1>`. `start_session` then launches pid2 in the same cwd; when session 2's transcript appears, the candidate set is `[pid1, pid2]` with pid1 claimed by session 1, so the claim-aware pick is pid2. Two rows, two pids, no overlap.

This stays `full` rather than `bug`: every spec-required observable is produced correctly on the path the recipe exercises. The residual is an ordering assumption, recorded in `caveats`.

## driver_capability = ready

`driver_step_types_from_file replaydata/agents/copilot/driver-interactive.sh` reports `exit_clean interrupt keys reset_session restart resume send session sigkill slash sleep start_session wait_turn` — `start_session` and `session` are both present and real (not `not_implemented` stubs): `start_session) save_active; launch_repl ;;` and `session) save_active; load_slot "$(jq -r '.session // 1' <<<"$step")" ;;`.

The driver is already written for concurrency rather than merely tolerant of it:

- `launch_repl` calls `alloc_slot "copilotdrv-$$-…-$((N_SLOTS + 1))" "$RUN_CWD"`, so slot 2 launches into the SAME `RUN_CWD` as slot 1 — which is precisely what this scenario needs, and what makes both processes cwd-match.
- `resolve_transcript` resolves the new session by SET DIFFERENCE against a `PRE_LAUNCH_DIRS` snapshot taken immediately before each launch, with an in-source comment naming this case: "a concurrent session (or a leftover from an earlier slot) makes 'newest' the wrong answer." Slot 1's directory is inside the snapshot, so slot 2 resolves to its own.
- `seed_copilot_home` rewrites only `config.json` (it does not touch `session-state/`), so re-running it at slot 2's launch cannot disturb session 1's transcript.
- `wait_ready` answers the folder-trust modal per launch, so slot 2 is not blocked even though the modal reappears for an already-trusted folder on 1.0.77.

## Spec-anchoring choice

Every phase anchors on a WORKING transition, never on a `ready`. Copilot is a presession adapter (the `2-1_basic-turn` sibling models `presession_birth` → `session_birth` explicitly): the process exists while the session directory still holds only `workspace.yaml`, so `processlifecycle.Scanner` mints a born-ready `proc-<PID>` row before the fswatcher can see any transcript. With TWO processes there are up to two such placeholders in flight, and a `ready`-anchored `new_session` phase would greedily bind to whichever placeholder appeared first. `proc-*` rows never enter `working`, so working-anchoring skips them deterministically. This is the same anchoring kiro-cli's sibling cell uses for the same reason, and the miss the assess playbook warns about.

The two distinct session ids are asserted relationally (`new_session` / `same_session_as`) rather than literally, because Copilot mints its own UUID per launch and the driver does not get to choose it (`--session-id` exists but the recipe does not use it, keeping the recording faithful to an ordinary launch).

`model` is deliberately NOT pinned: `--model` accepts only `auto` on this account and `session.auto_mode_resolved` picks between `gpt-5-mini` and `claude-haiku-4.5` per turn, so an exact match would be nondeterministic across three turns. `tokens_nonzero` and `cost_nonzero` are asserted — `assistant.message` carries `outputTokens` and both reachable models are priced.
caveats: PROVISIONAL ON EMISSION: no live recording has yet put two copilot processes in one cwd. The daemon=full verdict is derived from the adapter source plus the services-layer two-sessions-same-cwd regression test, not from an observed events.jsonl. record promotes it from provisional to settled.

The claim-aware disambiguator's correctness here rests on 'highest PID == most recently launched' (narrowByCWD's documented macOS assumption). Under PID wraparound the second copilot process could get a LOWER pid than the first; if its proc-<PID> placeholder has already claimed it, claimAwareDisambiguate finds no unclaimed candidate and falls back to the highest claimed pid — session 1's — at which point cleanupStalePIDHolders would delete session 1's row. This is an agent-agnostic seam shared by every cwd-discovered adapter (kiro-cli, mistral-vibe), not a copilot regression, and it is not expected to fire in a recording where the two launches are seconds apart. If a recording DOES show a lost row or a swapped binding, this is the mechanism to look at first.

POSSIBLE UNLOCK if the cwd tie-break proves fragile: copilot writes an authoritative session-id-to-PID map to disk. app.js does registerSessionLock(sessionId, path) -> inUseLocksRegisterSession(sessionId, path, process.pid), and the 1-4_session-resume probe live-observed the resulting `inuse.<pid>.lock` inside the session's own directory. That is structurally the same signal claudecode's pid.go uses as its authoritative Layer 1 (~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json), and would let DiscoverPID bind by session id instead of cwd. Not wired today, and deliberately not proposed as part of this cell — noted so a future fix does not have to re-derive it. Note the lock is transient: with no copilot running, none of the live session directories under ~/.copilot/session-state/ contains an inuse.*.lock (inUseLocksRelease* sweeps them on exit), so a consumer would have to tolerate its absence.

The recipe spends THREE turns of the maintainer's AI credits (session 1 turn, session 2 turn, session 1 re-drive). The third turn is not padding — it is the only phase that proves the PID-to-session binding stayed stable while a rival process shared the cwd, so it cannot be dropped to save credits.

Copilot creates <uuid>/ at launch but writes events.jsonl only on the first prompt, so BOTH real session rows appear late relative to their processes. Between start_session and session 2's first prompt the dashboard legitimately shows session 1 plus a proc-<PID> placeholder, not two real rows. Any human eyeballing the recording should read that window as correct, not as a missing session.

DRIVER FOOTGUN, worked around in this recipe rather than fixed: the copilot driver's step loop dispatches on .type only (`type="$(jq -r '.type' <<<"$step")"`) and has no equivalent of claudecode's per-step retarget (`tgt=$(jq -r '.session // empty' <<<"$step")` -> save_active + load_slot). The claudecode and kiro-cli recipes for THIS scenario both tag the re-drive as {"type":"send","session":1}; copied verbatim onto copilot that field is inert and the re-drive would land on session 2, producing a recording that verifies green while proving nothing about PID stability. This recipe uses an explicit {"type":"session","session":1} step instead, which the driver does implement. Making the copilot driver honour the field too (five lines, mirroring claudecode) would remove the trap for every future copilot recipe.

cleanupPreSessionsForProject retires ALL proc-<pid> placeholders matching the project/cwd when a real session for that cwd arrives, and the periodic sweep's matchCWD path does the same after a 90s grace. With two live processes in one cwd, session 1's arrival can therefore retire a placeholder belonging to session 2's still-unidentified process. This only removes a transient placeholder row — the real session 2 row still arrives and still binds its own pid — and the spec's working-anchored phases are blind to it by design.

sources.note: DiscoverPID = processlifecycle.DiscoverPIDByCWD(ProcessName, cwd, disambiguate) — cwd-only, no argv filter, no sidecar. This is the cell's crux: two same-cwd processes both match and the disambiguator decides.

Source: FilesUnderRoot{Dir: sessionsDir(), SessionIDFromPath: sessionIDFromPath, Parser: JSONLineParser{NewParser: () => &Parser{}}}. Session id comes from the <uuid> directory, so two launches are two rows; a fresh stateful Parser per file means the two sessions share no parser state. Process.Match = ExactName{"copilot"} (the native child, not the node loader).

claimAwareDisambiguate: highest UNCLAIMED cwd candidate, falling back to highest claimed. TryDiscoverPID returns early when state.PID > 0, so a bound session is never rediscovered. cleanupStalePIDHolders deletes any other non-subagent holder of a newly claimed pid — the mechanism that both retires the proc-<PID> placeholder and, under the wraparound caveat, could delete a live sibling.

The adapter-agnostic regression test for this exact crux: two EventNewSessions with the same CWD, the second discovered after the first has bound, asserting different PIDs with sess-a==1001 ('highest unclaimed') and sess-b==1000 ('1001 already claimed'). Copilot reaches this code through the same DiscoverPIDByCWD path.

narrowByCWD canonicalises cwd via EvalSymlinks then filters by exact CWDOf match, delegating multi-match resolution to the caller's disambiguate; its own highestPID default ('most recently started on macOS') is the documented assumption behind the PID-wraparound caveat.
cleanupPreSessionsForProject retires every proc-<pid> pre-session for the arriving real session's project/cwd — the basis for the transient-placeholder caveat in a shared-cwd recording.

CLI 1.0.77 shipped bundle. Create path: `let y=nf(p.sessionId,d),S=await this.registerSessionLock(p.sessionId,y);p.alreadyInUse=S`; `registerSessionLock(e,n){return await h.inUseLocksRegisterSession(e,n,process.pid)}`. Every lock primitive is session-keyed (inUseLocksRegister/RegisterSession/Release/ReleaseAllSessions/ReleaseSession/Sweep) and checkSessionsInUse takes {sessionIds}. Grep for workspaceLock|lockWorkspace|directoryLock|cwdLock returns nothing; the sole 'already running for: ${this.targetWorkspaceFolder}' is an in-process guard on the IDE lock-file watcher (`start(){if(this.watcher)return …}`). Hence no cwd-level exclusion on a second concurrent launch.

DRIVE_ELICITS includes start_session and session; both arms are implemented (start_session -> save_active + launch_repl; session -> `save_active; load_slot "$(jq -r '.session // 1' <<<"$step")"`). The step loop (`while IFS= read -r step; do type="$(jq -r '.type' <<<"$step")"`) dispatches on .type ONLY — unlike claudecode's driver, which additionally retargets on a per-step .session field; the shared replaydata/_lib/drive/slots.sh provides save_active/load_slot but no such hook. Hence this recipe's explicit session step. launch_repl allocs each slot with RUN_CWD so slot 2 shares slot 1's cwd, and re-snapshots PRE_LAUNCH_DIRS before every launch so resolve_transcript takes a set difference — its comment names the concurrent-session case explicitly. seed_copilot_home rewrites only config.json, never session-state/.

Live probe on 1.0.77 that observed `inuse.<pid>.lock` written into the session's own directory, and confirmed copilot mints a brand-new session-state/<uuid>/ on every launch. Basis for the 'possible unlock' caveat and for 'a launch always mints its own session directory'.

Sibling cell establishing copilot's presession shape (proc-<PID> born ready before events.jsonl exists, real session reconciling under a different id) and the observation vector reused here: tokens_nonzero + cost_nonzero asserted, model left unpinned because --model accepts only "auto".
Template for the working-anchored phase shape used here — the sibling cwd-discovered adapter that solved the same born-ready proc-<PID> greedy-match problem for this scenario.

preconditions: GitHub Copilot CLI 1.0.77 on PATH and authenticated (credentials live in the OS keychain, so COPILOT_HOME isolation needs no re-login)
An active Copilot plan with AI credits — this recipe spends THREE turns (session 1, session 2, session 1 again)
irrlichd is recording — run-cell.sh in isolated mode, or --attach against a daemon started with --record
No OTHER copilot process shares the staging cwd: the recipe deliberately creates exactly two, and a third would make the cwd tie-break ambiguous
setup: The driver seeds a scratch COPILOT_HOME under staging with trustedFolders + askedSetupTerminals pre-answered; each session directory is minted under $COPILOT_HOME/session-state/<session-id>/

The start_session step launches session 2 (slot 2) via a second `copilot --no-color --allow-all` in the SAME <staging>/cwd, keeping session 1 alive — this is what puts two processes behind one cwd for DiscoverPIDByCWD

wait_ready answers the folder-trust modal on each launch (it reappears on 1.0.77 even for an already-trusted folder), and resolve_transcript resolves slot 2 by set difference against the pre-launch directory snapshot so it cannot latch onto slot 1's directory

An EXPLICIT {"type":"session","session":1} step routes the following send/wait_turn back to session 1 while session 2 stays alive — the PID-stability re-drive. NOTE this differs from the claudecode/kiro-cli recipes for this scenario, which tag the send itself with a "session" FIELD: the copilot driver's step loop dispatches purely on .type and has no per-step .session retarget, so a field-tagged send would silently drive session 2 and the cell would prove nothing

script.text: Reply with exactly the word: alpha
Reply with exactly the word: bravo
Reply with exactly the word: alpha2

verify: events.jsonl contains 2 distinct copilot session ids (two <uuid> directories under the scratch COPILOT_HOME/session-state), both bound to the same cwd
each session id has its own independent working->ready arc; no transition on one is attributed to the other
session 1 shows TWO working->ready arcs (turn 1 + the post-start_session re-drive); session 2 shows ONE — proving session 1 stayed bound and independent while session 2 was alive
pid_discovered binds a DIFFERENT copilot PID to each session (the claim-aware disambiguator's highest-unclaimed pick over the two same-cwd candidates)
no state flapping: the daemon never swaps the PID-to-session binding between the two rows, and neither real session row is deleted by the other's PID claim
any proc-<PID> placeholder rows are transient and retired once their real session arrives; the recording settles at exactly two real session rows
observation vector: tokens_nonzero=true, cost_nonzero=true; model left unasserted (auto-router picks per turn)
